request.reason: record source references supplied with the prepared Work Item start

acceptanceCriteria: Same raw bytes and the same complete evidence observation binding are idempotent; corrected source metadata or a new collection observation at the same raw digest is appended under a distinct observation identity without replacing raw bytes or the existing receipt.

A consumer can explicitly select and bind the intended observation version; unsupported older Runtime versions reject the new selector instead of silently ignoring it, while legacy v1/v2/v3 inputs and outputs keep their existing interpretation.

The observation binding includes every identity/source/runtime-relevant field except generated now; raw digest remains the byte identity; existing source, assurance, freshness, Git, resource, and Runtime checks are not relaxed.
Parsed evidence/selector objects flow through validation and persistence; no serialization round trip can drop or reinterpret the selector.

Publication is no-replace and atomic; repeated identical imports are idempotent; concurrent conflicting writes, malformed records, cross-Work-Item bindings, tampered raw bytes, wrong source, stale evidence, and ambiguous selectors fail closed.

Historical evidence remains readable without migration; tests prove legacy compatibility, append-only corrections, exact selector binding, idempotency, concurrency behavior, and negative validation cases.
previousContract.goal: Allow a corrected or freshly collected delegated-evidence observation to coexist with the original when raw SHA-256 is unchanged, bind consumers to an explicit versioned observation selector, retain strict source and assurance checks, and preserve legacy v1/v2/v3 behavior.
previousContract.intent: Support repeat collection and source correction for delegated evidence with identical raw bytes while preserving immutable observation history.
outOfScope: close or cleanup records; generic migration or database work; provider network fetching or authentication; changes that weaken raw digest
or Runtime validation; cross-history finalization-chain upgrades; merge
